rows.label: Concept
rows.text: ## Living inside the theme Technology is the one unit you can research by looking up: the phone in your hand is simultaneously the library, the classroom and the distraction. That double life is the theme — the same device that delivered this course to your village can deliver the rumour that empties it.…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text:
Balance is the theme: benefits (communication, access) vs harms (addiction, privacy).
Use examples of digital etiquette when answering communication questions.

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: ## The debates, held honestly Four arguments run through every version of this theme, and each deserves its real shape rather than a slogan. **Attention.** The feed is not a service sold to you; it is you, sold to advertisers — which is why it is engineered to never end. The fix is not willpower alone but design: timers, greyscale, bedrooms without chargers.…  ·  ## Grammar and style: writing about the always-on present Digital life lives in two tenses and the essay must hold both. The **present simple** states the system's truths — "the algorithm **prioritises** engagement over accuracy" — while the **present continuous** tracks the drift of the moment: "students **are increasingly relying** on AI tutors; teachers **are rewriting** their assessments." Mixing them carelessly…

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: ## How the exam asks it The **advantages/disadvantages essay** ("Impact of mobile phones on students") wants two real benefits and two real costs and then a judgement — never a list of five vague blessings. The **problem–solution task** ("Cyberbullying among teenagers") wants causes before cures and solutions at three levels — individual, family, school or law.…  ·  **Technology: boon and bane (classified)** | Domain | Benefit | Cost | |---|---|---| | Communication | Instant, global | Shallow contact | | Learning | Anytime access | Distraction engines | | Work | Automation of drudgery | Job displacement | | Health | Better diagnostics | Screen-time illness |

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: ## The words that carry the theme Digital English is built on **phrasal verbs**, and the particles carry the meaning: you *log in* and *log out*, *sign up for* an account, *back up* your files (because drives die at exam time), *hack into* an account, *run out of* battery mid-sentence, *look up* a word, *cut down on* screen time.…  ·  ## Reading the theme like a writer — the devices of the digital age The platforms are built on **metaphor**, and the metaphors flatter: a *wall* you write on, *friends* you may never meet, a *cloud* that is actually a field of humming servers in a dry valley.…

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Trick 1: Technology questions demand balance: name TWO benefits and TWO harms, then take a stance — the 'both faces' pattern is the top band.  ·  Trick 2: Vocabulary matters: artificial intelligence, digital divide, screen time — use the unit's own terms in your answers.

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: Q. Is social media more harmful than helpful? (2 marks) — connectivity vs addiction/misinformation; conclude with your stance.
